title: The Pique Technique
description: An unusual request is more likely to be granted than a normal one.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Asking for something strange — "can I borrow 37 pence?" rather than "can I borrow some change?" — markedly increases compliance. The oddness interrupts the automatic refusal.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: A peculiar request does not match the script people use to dismiss everyday asks. It forces a moment of genuine thought, and during that pause the request is considered rather than deflected.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: A stranger asking for a specific, odd amount is helped more often than one asking for change.
An unusual opening question in a survey raises response rates.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: A request with an oddly specific detail.
A question that makes you stop and think before answering.

sections.title: Ethical Uses
sections.content: Being specific and clear about exactly what you need is genuinely better communication.

sections.title: Manipulative Uses
sections.content: Using novelty to bypass a considered "no".

sections.title: Red Flags
content: A request designed to feel unusual for no reason.
Oddness that disappears once you engage.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Answer the request as if it were ordinary — would you say yes anyway?
Notice when novelty is doing the persuading.

sections.title: Mistakes People Make
content: Treating the strange detail as the point.
Answering before you have actually considered it.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: Judge the request, not the oddity.
